subject: Discovery recap: Migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models (Shoply)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Smith <evan.smith@shoply.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Hi Evan / Olivia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. As promised, a short recap of what we heard, success criteria you mentioned, and recommended next steps so we’re all aligned before a PoC. I’ve attached a short PDF and a model shortlist spreadsheet.

Summary of pain points (as discussed)
- High and unpredictable token costs with current usage patterns (completions + embeddings).
- Rate limits and throttling during heavy batch ingestion windows — impacts offline workflows and real-time search.
- Latency spikes for interactive flows (chat + tool-calling) during peak traffic.
- Vendor lock concerns: reliance on closed APIs makes audits and on-prem options difficult.
- Need parity for streaming, function/tool calls, and embedding vector compatibility (existing index + retriever).

Current stack (what you shared)
- Primary: OpenAI (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini) for chat/completions; Anthropic for safety-sensitive classification.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for semantic search and re-ranking, stored in Pinecone.
- Traffic: ~6M tokens/day average, spikes to ~20M tokens/day during batch jobs.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile < 300ms for chat prompt-response; online pipelines require streaming token-by-token.

Success criteria for migration (you highlighted)
- Cost reduction target: >= 40% unit cost reduction for generation/embedding workload.
- Performance: maintain or improve 95th percentile latency for chat flows.
- Compatibility: function/tool-calling and streaming parity so product changes are minimal.
- Quality: <= 5% degradation on your evaluation prompts (we’ll run your eval set).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and VPC/private deployment options for sensitive data.

Model shortlist (initial recommendation for PoC)
- Llama 2 (13B, 70B) — good ecosystem support and proven for instruction tuning.
- Mistral (7B/8B variants) — strong cost/performance for chat & generation.
- Falcon-40B-instruct — larger context and strong instruction-following.
- Mistral Instant / Mistral Large mixture — candidate for low-latency inference.
- Open embeddings alternatives: SBERT variants and local quantized embedding models (for parity testing).

Key compatibility checks we recommend including in the PoC
- API parity: mimic OpenAI-style completions + chat + function-calling semantics.
- Streaming: verify token-by-token streaming and reconnect/fall-back behavior.
- Embedding vector drift: run embedding comparators against your Pinecone indexes.
- Quantization & latency tests: measure cost/throughput across 8-bit/4-bit configs.
- Safety stack: port the Anthropic classification steps into the pipeline and validate false-positive/negative rates.

Proposed next steps
1) PoC scope (2-week): run generation + embeddings benchmarks on a representative subset (we suggest ~50k prompts + 10k embedding vectors).
2) Provide your eval prompts & re-ranker slices (Olivia — can you share a CSV of the top 2k prompts?).
3) Security: we’ll send SOC2 and PoC-hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
4) Logistics: procurement & billing contacts (Aditya — looping you in).
5) Kickoff: propose Tue 23 Jun for a 30-min technical kickoff to align infra and data access.

Files attached: redwood-discovery-recap.pdf, model-shortlist.xlsx

If I missed anything or you want this written differently, say the word and I’ll update the recap.

Best,

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

---

From: Evan Smith <evan.smith@shoply.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@shoply.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: the 6M tokens/day is the current average; the 20M/day spikes are mostly monthly batch jobs (product ingest). For PoC please include a batch ingestion simulation.
- Embeddings: we use text-embedding-3-small exclusively today; downstream retrievers expect 1536-d vectors.
- Tool calling: we rely heavily on function-calls for structured DB writes (order events). Function signatures must be preserved or we’ll need a lightweight shim.
- Security: SOC2 report would be good; for private deployment we’ll need to validate KMS integration.

We can share the 2k eval prompts — Olivia will drop them into the drive you shared.

For the PoC window, we’d like to include a simple A/B traffic split in production for 10% of sessions if the initial latency checks out — is that feasible from your end?

Thanks — Evan

---
Evan Smith
Head of ML Platforms | Shoply
evan.smith@shoply.com | +1 (206) 555-8899

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Smith <evan.smith@shoply.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Evan — all noted. Short replies inline: 

- Batch ingest: included in PoC scope. We’ll run a synthetic batch job matching your peak patterns and report latency/cost delta.
- Embedding dims: we’ll include a compatibility check with 1536-d vectors. If a model’s native embeddings differ, we’ll run mapping and evaluate re-ranker impact.
- Function calling: we’ll validate function-call parity and provide a small shim option if needed; aim is minimal product changes.
- A/B 10% traffic: feasible. For safety we recommend starting with an internal-only mirrored traffic test, then Canary 1% -> 10% if metrics look good.

Next steps: I’ll circulate a PoC scope doc (attached: PoC-scope.docx) and set up the Tues 23 Jun kickoff for 11:00 PT. Rishi will lead the technical kickoff and be your main SE contact. Aditya will drive procurement and contract questions.

One ask for Olivia/Evan: please upload the eval prompt CSV and a small sample of your embedding vectors (10k) to the shared drive by EOD Monday 22 Jun so we can stage the index.

—
Marissa

Attachments: PoC-scope.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Looping in procurement notes:

- Aditya, FYI: Shoply indicated they may want a private deployment option if the PoC meets security checks. Please prepare standard dedicated/private pricing tiers and include SOC2/HIPAA options. I attached our current SOC2 attestation for Shoply to reference.
- Marissa: I’ll prepare a checklist for infra access (SSH keys, VPC peering options, KMS requirements).

Evan — I’ll be on the kickoff 23 Jun and will bring a short test plan: connectivity, streaming latency tests, function-call parity, and embedding comparators. If Shoply can provision the sample data ahead of time that will shave a day off the setup.

Thanks,
Rishi
